# Model & Reasoning Effort — One Strong Model, Max Effort, Everywhere

_Applies when: always — every session and every delegated subagent / Workflow, regardless of task size._

**One strong model for both strands, at maximal effort on both.** There is no session-vs-delegation
cost split: the interactive chat and every delegated subagent run the same model.

## Which model — most reliable for agentic work, not the newest or nominally strongest

The session model is the one most **reliable for agentic, long-horizon work** — currently **Opus**,
the product's own default. Ranking is not the criterion; fitness for delegated, tool-heavy work is —
a higher tier can top the charts and still cost double, force data retention, and never return its
raw chain of thought. **Fable 5 is that tier, so it is never automatic** (ADR-0037): not the session
model, not a delegation model, not an `llm-council` member, never a `model` parameter in the Agent
tool or a Workflow — using it needs the user's **explicit prior consent**, asked first, not reported after.

## Both strands

- **The interactive session** — the chat a human starts by hand (the CLI / IDE strand) — runs that
  model at the **highest persistable effort**. It is the orchestrator and always runs at full
  strength; **never downgrade it**.
- **Delegated subagents and Workflow fan-out** run the **same** model at **max effort**, every agent
  alike — there are **no cheap or low-tier workers** and **no per-role tiering**.

## Relation to token discipline (`25-orchestration`)

- Token discipline caps the **number** of agents and favors cheap inline **thinking**; it **never**
  weakens the **effort** of work that actually runs, and it does not pick the model.
- Minimize how many agents you fan out and prefer inline reading/planning over spawning an agent —
  then run whatever does run at full effort. Fewer agents, each at max effort.
- Process ceremony (Bugfix / Lite / Full in `20-workflow`) scales **team size, not effort**: a
  one-file bugfix is still done at max effort — delegated to an agent, or inline in the session —
  never at reduced effort.

## Where the concrete IDs live

Concrete per-target model IDs live in each target's own config — the interactive CLI/IDE target via
its agent-core-managed `settings.json` (ADR-0033, seeded not forced per ADR-0013); OpenCode runs
entirely on the internal provider network via `opencode.json` plus the OpenCode-only rule
`62-model-effort-opencode` (ADR-0011).
